index.title: Docs
index.description: Reference and live examples for @gridkitjs/react and @gridkitjs/core.
index.intro: GridKit is early: the API is still moving and may break between minor versions. These docs cover what's shipped today and run against the real, published packages.

overview.title: @gridkitjs/react
overview.description: React components for GridKit, built on @gridkitjs/core.
overview.intro: @gridkitjs/react renders semantic class names — gridkit-data-grid, header-cell, grid-row — and carries no styles of its own. Pair it with @gridkitjs/theme-tailwind, or target the same class names with your own stylesheet.

dataGrid.title: DataGridComponent
dataGrid.description: The grid component: columns, data, borders, resizing, reordering, and selection.
dataGrid.intro: DataGridComponent takes a set of columns and a data source and renders a grid. Resizing, reordering, and selection are all opt-in — enable them per grid with resizableColumns, reorderableColumns, and selectable, or per column via each column's own resizable and reorderable fields.

events.title: Events
events.description: The callbacks DataGridComponent fires as a user resizes, reorders, and selects.
events.intro: Every interaction reports through a callback prop rather than a ref or an event you have to subscribe to. Resizing and reordering fire one each; selection fires thirteen, one per row, column, and cell transition plus a whole-selection change to persist from.

columnTemplates.title: Column templates
columnTemplates.description: Custom header and cell rendering with headerTemplate and cellTemplate.
columnTemplates.intro: Start from defineColumnsFromRows for the columns you don't need to customize, then declare the ones you do. headerTemplate and cellTemplate accept any React node, so formatting and conditional styling are plain component code.

columnResizing.title: Column resizing
columnResizing.description: Dragging a column wider with resizableColumns, resizeMode, and columnSizeDefaults.
columnResizing.intro: resizableColumns turns on dragging a header's trailing edge to resize, unless a column sets its own resizable to override the grid. Double-clicking the edge fits the column to its content instead. resizeMode decides what happens to the rest of the grid: "fit" (the default) redistributes the space a resize gives up or takes among the other columns; "fixed" leaves every other column exactly where it was.

columnReordering.title: Column reordering
columnReordering.description: Dragging a column into a new position with reorderableColumns.
columnReordering.intro: reorderableColumns turns on dragging a header to a new position, unless a column sets its own reorderable to override the grid. A column that can't move can still be moved past — dragging one past a fixed column is fine, only the fixed one can't itself be picked up.
columnReordering.exampleHeading: Drag a header to reorder it

columnSelection.title: Column selection
columnSelection.description: Letting the user select whole columns with selectable.columns.
columnSelection.intro: selectable.columns takes false, "single", or "multiple" — off by default, since selection claims the click a display-only grid shouldn't. A column click replaces the selection, Ctrl-click toggles one column in or out, and Shift-click takes every column between the last click and this one.

rowSelection.title: Row selection
rowSelection.description: Letting the user select whole rows with selectable.rows.
rowSelection.intro: selectable.rows takes false, "single", or "multiple" — off by default, since selection claims the click a display-only grid shouldn't. Give getRowId alongside it for data that sorts, filters, or pages; without one a row is identified by its position, so a re-sort leaves the same positions selected under different rows.

cellSelection.title: Cell selection
cellSelection.description: Letting the user select one cell at a time with selectable.cells.
cellSelection.intro: selectable.cells takes only false or "single": a cell addresses one value, so there is no "multiple" and no range to take. A click moves the selection to that cell; Ctrl-click on the selected cell clears it.

overview.title: @gridkitjs/core
overview.description: Framework-agnostic grid logic: column inference, ordering, resizing, and selection.
overview.intro: @gridkitjs/core is plain TypeScript — so it's testable without a DOM and reusable from other framework adapters. Today it covers column inference, ordering, resizing, and selection; sorting, filtering, and paging are not implemented yet.

columnDefinitions.title: Column definitions
columnDefinitions.description: Inferring columns from row data with defineColumnsFromRows.
columnDefinitions.intro: defineColumnsFromRows inspects your row data and infers a type and alignment per field, one level into nested objects. Use it as a starting point, then override or extend individual columns.

resizing.title: Resizing
resizing.intro: resolveColumnWidths and fitColumnsToWidth are the functions DataGridComponent calls internally when resizableColumns is enabled — the first resolves each column's width from its definition, the sizing state, and the grid's defaults, the second redistributes width across columns under resizeMode="fit". Reach for them directly if you're building a custom grid adapter.
resizing.exampleHeading: The same logic, in the React grid

ordering.title: Ordering
ordering.intro: applyColumnOrder and moveColumnBefore are the functions DataGridComponent calls internally when reorderableColumns is enabled — the first puts a column list in the order an order state gives, the second moves one column id to sit before another. Reach for them directly if you're building a custom grid adapter.
ordering.exampleHeading: The same logic, in the React grid

selection.title: Selection
selection.intro: These transforms are what a click, a Ctrl-click, and a Shift-click each reduce to — every one takes the selection it received and returns the selection after, never touching a DOM node or a row of data. @gridkitjs/react calls them from useGridSelection; a second framework binding can call them the same way.
selection.exampleHeading: The same logic, in the React grid

overview.title: @gridkitjs/theme-tailwind
overview.description: Palette tokens, dark mode, and the grid's styles.
overview.intro: @gridkitjs/react renders semantic class names — gridkit-data-grid, header-cell, grid-row — and this stylesheet targets them directly. Nothing needs to scan component source, and every colour is a CSS custom property, so overriding one is plain CSS.
